newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Lippo backs Hong Kong as foreign base.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Lippo backs Hong Kong as foreign base.

text.p: The Lippo group expects Hong Kong to remain as its international base outside Indonesia and is comfortable with the prospect of the colony's reversion to China next year, Lippo Deputy Chairman James Riady said on Monday.
A company expanding outside Indonesia needed an international base "where as a foreigner you are treated exactly the same as a local", he told Reuters in an interview.
"I think Hong Kong is the only place in Asia that can do that. Hong Kong is also a financial centre, most companies around the world do have representatives in Hong Kong.

"It is also the gateway to mainland China...many people are fundamentally comfortable about mainland China, and therefore so about Hong Kong," he said, adding Lippo was "firm" about its position there.

The Indonesian conglomerate, with interests ranging from banking, insurance and securities to manufacturing, property, retailing and health care, has major financial and property interests in Hong Kong.

Riady said Lippo would also expand its presence in China itself, adding that "no Asian company can be truly regional if they're not in mainland China". It would also look to expand its presence in Singapore.
He said that of the five emerging Asian economies -- China, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and the Philippines -- China and Indonesia currently offered the best prospects.
He viewed China "more on a long-term basis" due to short term political and economic uncertainty.
Indonesia's short-term prospects were clear, despite investor concerns over July riots in Jakarta, which he said were overplayed.

"I think what we're seeing here in Indonesia is the government focussing consistently on the thing that is most important -- an open economy, a market-oriented economy...totally free exchange environment, fiscal responsibility, continued deregulation.
"So I would say that the fundamentals haven't changed."
Riady said a planned restructuring of Lippo's financial group that is due to go before an extraordinary general meeting on Friday was designed to take advantage of Indonesia's economic growth.

"We continue to feel that Indonesia is still the best place for investments...and knowing that the financial services group of Lippo is still our main business, we want to do a financial structuring that would in effect create synergy between the banking, the life insurance and our investment (securities) business," he said.
He expected the restructuring, which involves Lippo Bank, Lippo Life and Lippo Securities, would be of long-term benefit to the group's shareholders.
"At the bank's level...our earnings will be boosted even into a better level. The life (insurance) would be in a much more solid position," he said.
